papers.title: Next-Generation Bioplastics for Food Packaging: Sustainable Materials and Applications
papers.authors: Shi, X., Cui, L., Xu, C., & Wu, S.
papers.relevanceSummary: Synthesizes recent advances in next-generation food-packaging bioplastics, evaluating mechanical performance, barrier engineering, and practical food-sector adoption pathways.

papers.title: An Overview of Bio-Based Polymers with Potential for Food Packaging Applications
papers.authors: Şomoghi, R., Mihai, S., & Oancea, F.
papers.relevanceSummary: Provides a broad comparative overview of bio-based polymer families (polyesters and polysaccharides), linking polymer origins and processing routes to food-packaging suitability.

papers.title: Tailoring the Barrier Properties of PLA: A State-of-the-Art Review for Food Packaging Applications
papers.authors: Marano, S., Laudadio, E., Minnelli, C., & Stipa, P.
papers.relevanceSummary: Examines strategies to overcome PLA's moderate water vapour and gas barrier limitations—including crystallinity control, blending, nanocomposites, and coatings—for food shelf-life extension.

papers.title: Current Research and Applications of Starch-Based Biodegradable Films for Food Packaging
papers.authors: Onyeaka, H., Obileke, K., Makaka, G., & Nwokolo, N.
papers.relevanceSummary: Reviews thermoplastic starch (TPS) film preparation, plasticization, moisture-sensitivity challenges, and mechanical/barrier improvements for dry and short-shelf-life food packaging.

papers.title: Bioplastics for Food Packaging: Environmental Impact, Trends and Regulatory Aspects
papers.authors: Cruz, R. M. S., et al.
papers.relevanceSummary: Connects bioplastic food-packaging innovation with life-cycle environmental impacts, food-contact migration safety, waste-management trends, and regulatory compliance frameworks.

papers.title: Design, New Materials, and Production Challenges of Bioplastics-Based Food Packaging
papers.authors: Rosenow, P., Fernández-Ayuso, C., López-García, P., & Minguez-Enkovaara, L. F.
papers.relevanceSummary: Addresses industrial scale-up constraints, thermal processing windows, structural design, and cost/manufacturing bottlenecks when transitioning bioplastics into commercial food packaging.

papers.title: Biopolymer-Based Sustainable Food Packaging Materials: Challenges, Solutions, and Applications
papers.authors: Perera, K. Y., Jaiswal, A. K., & Jaiswal, S.
papers.relevanceSummary: Evaluates polysaccharide and polyester biopolymers (including chitosan, alginate, cellulose, starch, PLA, and PHA), detailing mechanical/hydrophilic limitations and active-packaging solutions.

papers.title: Biodegradable Polymers for Food Packaging: A Review
papers.authors: Siracusa, V., Rocculi, P., Romani, S., & Dalla Rosa, M.
papers.relevanceSummary: Foundational review categorizing biodegradable food-packaging polymers (PLA, PHA/PHB, starch, cellulose, chitosan, alginate systems), summarizing mechanical, gas/water barrier, and processing considerations.

papers.title: Application of Bioplastics for Food Packaging
papers.authors: Peelman, N., Ragaert, P., De Meulenaer, B., Adons, D., Peeters, R., Cardon, L., et al.
papers.relevanceSummary: Evaluates practical food-packaging performance of bio-based polymers (PLA, PHB/PHBV, TPS, cellulose derivatives), emphasizing WVTR, optical clarity, migration compliance, and barrier-coating requirements across food categories.

papers.title: Biodegradation of Bioplastics in Natural Environments
papers.authors: Emadian, S. M., Onay, T. T., & Demirel, B.
papers.relevanceSummary: Compares biodegradation kinetics of PLA, PHA/PHB, and starch-based bioplastics across controlled composting, soil, freshwater, and marine environments, demonstrating why industrial compostability differs from ambient natural degradation.
